Article Title: 'Whitewashing history': Shiv Sena Shinde faction leaders tear up a copy of Sonia Gandhi's memoir
Article Text:
Shinde Sena leaders tear Sonia's memoir in symbolic protest

NEW DELHI: The Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena on Wednesday staged a symbolic protest against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's recently released memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', accusing her of "whitewashing history" and "denigrating Veer Savarkar".Led by Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC, party leaders, including Sanjay Nirupam and Anand Dubey, tore pages from the book during a demonstration in Mumbai.They also demanded that publisher HarperCollins remove passages on pages 201 and 443.Addressing a presser, Shaina accused Sonia Gandhi of insulting Savarkar by describing him as a "Hindutva exclusionary"."Sonia Gandhi humiliates Savarkar. She calls him a Hindutva exclusionary. But Balasaheb Thackeray always said that Savarkar is the soul of Hindutva," she said.Taking aim at Sonia Gandhi's journey to acquiring Indian citizenship, Shaina said, "Sonia ji, it took you 15-plus years to even initiate the process of Indian citizenship. Savarkar gave 50-plus years of his life, not just in jail, but also for the cause of Bharat. Who are you to judge?""You write a book; welcome to that. You try to whitewash history; we will not allow that.You cannot rewrite Savarkar's sacrifice. Maharashtra will never forgive you," she added.Demanding the removal of the passages, Shaina said, "We demand that HarperCollins eliminate pages 201 and 443. Savarkar spent 11 years in Kala Pani for India's freedom. Balasaheb Thackeray worshipped Savarkar."She also questioned Sonia Gandhi's understanding of the RSS and India's freedom struggle, asking, "Do you know the ABC of the RSS? Do you know the ABC of nation-building and the sacrifice that crores of Indians have given at the time of our freedom?"Sonia Gandhi's memoir was launched on Monday in the presence of political leaders from several parties. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were among those who attended the event.In the book, Sonia Gandhi reflects on her personal journey of settling in India, including the challenges of adapting to a new culture and unfamiliar surroundings.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', was launched on Monday. Shiv Sena leaders tore pages from the book during a demonstration in Mumbai. They accused Sonia Gandhi of "whitewashing history" and "denigrating Veer Savarkar"

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented a range of traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines, offering gifts that showcased the country's diverse regional craftsmanship, textile traditions and cultural heritage.The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. PM Modi also presented a Dokra artwork boat to Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Bidriware silver inlay vases to Myanmar and Brunei, a royal blue Banarasi silk stole to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and a Jaipur blue pottery artefact to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.The presents drew on traditional art forms and crafts from different parts of India, including Rajasthan, Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and the Deccan region.PM Modi gifted Trump a Golden Pichwaai painting from Nathdwara in Rajasthan. The traditional cloth-painting art is known for its intricate detailing, luminous colours and elaborate compositions.Created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments and gold detailing, Pichwaai paintings feature motifs such as lotuses, cows and trees, along with ornamental borders. Their golden finish gives the artwork a distinctive regal appearance.The Philippine President received a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet, a hand-knotted craft admired for its sheen, soft texture, intricate designs and durability.Made from fine silk, the carpets involve thousands of knots tied by skilled artisans. Some take months or even years to complete. Their designs often draw inspiration from Kashmir's natural beauty, featuring floral patterns, chinar leaves and geometric motifs.PM Modi presented a traditional Chola bronze sculpture to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The art form flourished between the ninth and thirteenth centuries under the Chola dynasty in South India.The sculptures are made using the traditional lost-wax casting technique, known as Madhuchista Vidhana. Each piece is individually handcrafted, making it unique.Known for their anatomical precision, graceful forms and expressive details, Chola bronzes also offer insights into the clothing, jewellery, hairstyles and artistic traditions of the period. They represent Tamil Nadu's metallurgical skills and artistic heritage.PM Modi gifted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim a traditional silver worked urli, a decorative Indian vessel adorned with intricate silver embellishments that showcase the skill of the country's metalworkers.Traditionally filled with water and decorated with floating flowers, the urli symbolises purity, prosperity, hospitality and harmony.Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet received a traditional Dokra artwork boat. The metal craft is made using the lost-wax casting technique, a tradition dating back more than 4,000 years.The handcrafted piece depicts a boat carrying figures and birds, reflecting community life and harmony with nature. Each artwork is individually modelled in wax before being cast in metal.The boat symbolises unity, cooperation, resilience and collective progress. The craft also preserves traditional skills and supports artisan livelihoods.PM Modi gifted Bidriware silver inlay vases from Bidar, Karnataka, to Myanmar and Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei.Bidriware is a traditional metal craft made from a zinc-and-copper alloy and decorated with intricate pure silver inlay. Artisans engrave patterns, insert silver wire and treat the surface to create its characteristic deep black finish, which contrasts with the silver designs.The floral and geometric motifs draw inspiration from the architectural heritage of Bidar Fort. The craft has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag and represents the artistic traditions of the Deccan region.Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole presented in a Sadheli box.Woven from fine Katan silk, the stole showcases the centuries-old textile traditions of Banaras. Its intricate motifs reflect the craftsmanship and precision of generations of weavers.The royal blue colour symbolises dignity, wisdom and harmony, while the presentation in a Sadheli box represents India's warmth and cultural esteem.PM Modi gifted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese a traditional Jaipur blue pottery artefact from Rajasthan.The craft is known for its glossy white surface and luminous cobalt-blue designs. Its pieces feature hand-painted floral patterns, birds, geometric motifs and decorative borders.PM Modi gifted Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone a rose quartz elephant with gold work, a decorative craft associated with Rajasthan's stone-carving centres, particularly Jaipur.The artwork is carved from natural rose quartz and polished to bring out its soft, translucent sheen. It is then decorated with intricate hand-painted gold detailing, floral motifs and traditional ornamental designs.Combining gemstone carving with miniature painting, the elephant symbolises strength, wisdom, dignity and royal grandeur in Indian tradition. Its gilded detailing reflects India's heritage of luxury handicrafts and royal decorative arts.Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul received a traditional Rogan art painting from Kutch, Gujarat. Practised by a handful of artisan families in Nirona village, Rogan art is a rare, centuries-old textile painting tradition.The technique uses a thick, elastic paint prepared by boiling castor oil and mixing it with natural pigments. Artisans create intricate designs freehand on fabric using a slender metal stylus. The cloth is then folded to transfer a symmetrical mirror image onto the other half.Traditionally used in bridal trousseaus and festive attire, Rogan art is known for its intricate patterns, geometric precision and craftsmanship. It represents Kutch's cultural heritage and the ingenuity of its artisans.PM Modi gifted Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão a handcrafted agate bowl from Khambhat, Gujarat. Made from agate, a semi-precious gemstone, each bowl has distinctive natural bands, colours and textures, making every piece unique.Khambhat has been a centre of agate processing and stone carving for centuries. Skilled artisans carefully cut, shape and polish the stone to create decorative and functional objects.Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung received a traditional Indian leather wall hanging, a handcrafted decorative artwork rooted in the country's folk-art heritage.Artisans soften and stretch treated leather before creating intricate designs through perforation, embossing and painting. The artworks feature floral, geometric and wildlife motifs, often made using natural vegetable dyes.Rooted in rural traditions and passed down through generations, the craft reflects regional artistic styles and storytelling. It also helps preserve traditional skills and support artisan livelihoods.The gifts were presented during PM Modi's November 16-17 visit to the Philippines, where he attended the 23rd Asean-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. He also participated in a Quad leaders' meeting with Trump, Takaichi and Albanese.During the visit, India and Asean adopted a joint statement on cooperation in disaster management. The two sides also agreed to strengthen early warning systems, share satellite data, conduct joint simulation exercises and promote the use of artificial intelligence in disaster risk assessment and response coordination.PM Modi announced several initiatives to deepen India's engagement with the region, including a maritime cooperation plan, a joint cyber forensics training programme, technical exchanges on nuclear energy, a space hackathon and cooperation on critical minerals.Other announcements included youth and start-up initiatives, enhanced scholarships for Asean students at Nalanda University and free e-visas for tourists from Asean countries.
Article Summary: PM Modi presented traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines. The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

Article Title: Ankita Bhandari case: Parents demand Vinod Arya's narco test, call details from night of murder

NEW DELHI: Ankita Bhandari's parents have demanded a narco test of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, father of the main accused Pulkit Arya in the 2022 murder case , and sought an examination of his call detail records (CDRs) from the night of the incident. They warned of protests across Uttarakhand until their demands are met.Speaking to the media on Tuesday, Ankita's father, Virendra Singh Bhandari, said Vinod Arya should also be investigated, alleging that he had repeatedly travelled between Delhi and Uttarakhand around the time of the murder. He urged the CBI to examine the matter, conduct Vinod Arya's narco test and retrieve his call details."I want that now we will not spare Vinod Arya either, and the CBI investigation into the policeman is going on, Vinod Arya's narco test will be done, and his call details will be extracted, because when the incident with my girl happened, even on that day I told the government and the police to arrest Vinod Arya first and send him to jail, because he was repeatedly going to Delhi and coming back from there," Virendra Singh Bhandari said.He further alleged that discussions involving senior political leaders were taking place in Delhi at the time and questioned the alleged VIP angle in the case.Referring to the appointment of former BJP Uttarakhand incharge Dushyant Kumar Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim, Virendra said the family had opposed the move and submitted a memorandum at India Gate in Delhi."The same thing happened that that VIP has been made the Governor of Sikkim today, and during that time too, as soon as I heard on October 12 that he has been made the Governor of Sikkim, immediately on October 14 we sat at India Gate and submitted a memorandum to His Excellency the National Council that until the investigation is fulfilled, Sikkim's Governor Dushyant Kumar Gautam should not be appointed, and despite that, on October 19 he was made the Governor of Sikkim," he said.Virendra also referred to recent remarks made by Vinod Arya about his daughter and reiterated the family's demand for a thorough probe, including a narco test and retrieval of call records. He warned that protests would continue across Uttarakhand until the demands were fulfilled."And the day before yesterday, just like Vinod Arya spoke nonsense about my girl, in the same way we want that now the CBI investigation that is going on should be done, Vinod Arya's narco test should be done, and his call details should be extracted, and across Uttarakhand, until his CBI investigation, his narco test and his call details are not extracted, we will protest across Uttarakhand," Virendra Bhandari said.The fresh demands come amid an escalating row over the alleged VIP angle in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case. On November 15, Vinod Arya demanded an investigation into Ankita's parents, alleging they had "harassed, humiliated, and coerced" her before the incident.Addressing a press conference in Haridwar, Arya cited a compilation of alleged chat logs running into around 4,800 pages and claimed his son was not mentioned in the conversations. He also appealed to Uttarakhand chief minister to take action against those who allegedly drove the 19-year-old to distress.Reiterating that there was no political angle or VIP involvement in the case, Arya said, "The chat consists of approximately 4,800 pages... to our knowledge, there is no VIP involved in this entire case. We have no connection to the elections, nor are we trying to steer the narrative. Our sole demand is that action be taken against those who harassed Ankita, which is her father and mother."Questioning the charges against resort staff, Arya claimed low-wage employees were unfairly implicated due to public pressure, which he alleged had led to severe tragedies in their families.Meanwhile, additional director general of police (Crime and Law & Order), Uttarakhand, V Murugesan, said police acted promptly in the case and arrested all three accused within 24 hours of the incident.Ankita's parents had earlier staged a sit-in at India Gate in Delhi opposing Dushyant Kumar Gautam's appointment as Sikkim Governor until the CBI probe was concluded. They were detained by police and later released from Tilak Marg Police Station.The case pertains to the September 2022 murder of 19-year-old Ankita, a receptionist at a resort near Rishikesh. Her family has opposed the appointment of anyone whose name surfaced during the investigation to a constitutional post without being cleared by investigative agencies.
Article Summary: Ankita Bhandari's parents demand a narco test of former BJP leader Vinod Arya. They also seek an examination of his call detail records (CDRs) from the night of the incident. They warned of protests across Uttarakhand until their demands are met.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice to a lawyer on a petition filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), seeking contempt action against him for making unsavoury remarks against CJI Surya Kant, news agency PTI reported.A three-judge bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought the lawyer's response to the plea."Having perused the papers before us, which include the consent of the AG under Section 15(1)(b) of the Contempt Act, we are prima facie satisfied that the motion of SCBA for initiation of pleading against the sole respondent referred in the petition requires to be taken forward. We issue notice returnable January 20, 2027," the bench said.Appearing for the SCBA, its president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai submitted that such conduct was totally unacceptable.The development comes after an unusual incident in the Supreme Court on Monday, when the lawyer was escorted out of the courtroom following his remarks against the CJI.The incident took place after a bench comprising the CJI and Justices Bagchi and Mohana assembled in the afternoon. The lawyer sought an urgent hearing on his submissions alleging corruption in the judiciary.He claimed that he had received no response from the CJI's office to a communication he had sent on November 2 regarding the issue and urged the court to hear him immediately."You cannot mention anything like this," Justice Mohana observed.When the lawyer persisted, the CJI said, "We will see, you just wait."However, the lawyer allegedly continued with his remarks against the CJI, saying, "No, I will not wait. You cannot sit in that chair. You do not deserve. You do not have the integrity for that."Following the exchange, virtual proceedings were suspended for some time.According to sources quoted by news agency PTI, security personnel later escorted the lawyer out of the courtroom.
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues notice to a lawyer on a petition filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association. The petition seeks contempt action against him for making unsavoury remarks against CJI Surya Kant. Article Title: SC upholds stay on Azam Khan's conviction; offers son, wife relief
Article Text:
SP leader Azam Khan and his family get relief in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta Azam Khan in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate and granted the same relief to Khan's son and wife, who were denied this benefit by the high court.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said all three were on the same footing and questioned the HC for discriminating among them. It said there was "apparent legal dichotomy in the judgement". It said, "We find that the HC failed to articulate any coherent legal reason why similar relief, as granted to Mohammad Azam Khan, was denied, even though all three were convicted under the self-same charge of conspiracy."Where several convicts standing on the same footing seek stay/suspension of conviction, it is legitimate for them to expect similar treatment... Parity being a facet of Article 14 of Constitution, equals ought to be treated equally unless, of course, an intelligible differentia having a rational nexus with the object of the order distinguishes one from the others," the bench said.SC said though differential treatment was not forbidden, "an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained". It said, "If the court grants a stay/suspension of conviction to one... while similar relief to other similarly situated convicts is denied, the distinguishing feature on the record must be identified and expressly stated as the reason for the departure from parity. An order silent on that point is, by itself, arbitrary. "
Article Summary: Supreme Court Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta Azam Khan in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said all three were on the same footing and questioned HC for discriminating among them.

Article Title: Indian inventor patents new technique to transmute elements, reports gold in tests
Article Text:
Bengaluru inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements, with lab tests reporting gold and silver in processed samples

How it works

.

Larger ambition

BENGALURU: What if one chemical element could be converted into several others, including gold? An Indian inventor from Bengaluru has received a patent for a process that could do this using specially generated frequencies, without conventional nuclear reactors or radioactive reactions.There is no fission or fusion reaction here. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples.Rajah Vijay Kumar’s invention, called Gravitoradiophysical Nuclear Transmutation (GNT), has been granted Indian patent (No. 5683222), nearly eight years after it was filed on Nov 21, 2017. The patent was granted in the second half of 2025.“The GNT could eventually find applications in energy, medicine, genetics, industry and space,” Kumar, director and chief scientific officer, Scalene Energy Research Institute, Organization de Scalene Foundation, told TOI.To understand the process, it helps to know what makes one element different from another. Every element has atoms, and at the centre of each atom is a nucleus. The number of protons in this nucleus determines the element’s identity.Gold, for example, has 79 protons, while mercury has 80. Turning mercury into gold would therefore require changing the structure of its nucleus by removing (or displacing) one proton and one electron, something an ordinary chemical reaction cannot do.Kumar’s proposed process uses a specially designed reactor to achieve this. Its central component, called the ‘Boom Tube’, a tubular reactor that produces continuous free fall and weightlessness at molecular levels, fitted with antennas made from an aluminium alloy and connected to a high power high frequency generator. The apparatus also has systems to regulate temperature and pressure in a vacuum environment.The process works in two proposed stages. First, one frequency is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. A second frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus.The process works in two proposed stages. First, a disassociating frequency depending on the interested elements is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. Then, an element specific transmutation frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus. The exact mechanism of action is still being studied.As Kumar explains: “Every element has a unique frequency, or set of frequencies, that can break its chemical bonds and separate it from a compound. For the initial experiments, I chose mercury, which it describes as one of the heavier elements that could be handled relatively safely in its experimental setup. The aim, however, was not simply to make gold.”The larger ambition was to develop a process that can convert different elements and isotopes for possible applications in energy, medicine, industry and space exploration.The patent describes experiments in which a mercury compound, mercuric sulphate, was mixed with distilled water and processed through the reactor. An untreated portion was retained for comparison. An accredited laboratory, reportedly unaware of which samples had been processed, analysed both.The results reported gold at 1.91 mg per litre in the first processed sample and 2.3 milligrams per litre in the second. Silver was also detected at 11 milligrams per litre in the second test. Other elements, including magnesium, manganese, phosphorus and zinc, were reported in the processed samples. The mercury came down from 33.45 gm to 8.67 gm while sulphur almost remained unchanged at around 8.5 gm.The laboratory used a technique called Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES), which identifies and measures the quantities of elements in a sample. The research team acknowledges that considerable work under different conditions remains before the process can be perfected or considered for large-scale applications.There is also an important scientific caveat. Detecting gold, silver or other elements in a sample does not, by itself, mean the technology or process is ready for wider use immediately. The laboratory technique measures what is present, not how it was formed. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly the science of how such claimed transmutation has occurred.
Article Summary: Inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly how such claimed transmutation has occurred.

Article Title: 'Again, I wasn't heard': Bilkis to fight SC order giving bail to 2 convicts
Article Text:
Bilkis Bano said she will challenge the SC's bail order for two convicts, alleging she was not informed or heard before the decision

After SC order, I'm scared once again for myself & family: Bilkis

Vadodara: Bilkis Bano has expressed shock and disbelief that the Supreme Court has without informing her, or giving her an opportunity to be heard, passed an order suspending the life sentences of and granting bail to two of 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and killing 14 of her family in the 2002 Gujarat riots She said this was the second time the court had done so. The first instance she referred to was May 2022, when the Supreme Court directed Gujarat's govt to consider the remission plea of convict Radheshyam Shah within two months. Bilkis was not made a party to those proceedings and not given an opportunity to object. The court subsequently declared that order a nullity in Jan 2024."I will fight this order. I must," Bilkis said in a statement issued through advocate Shobha Gupta. The family is said to have left Gujarat.Bilkis Bano said her fight was for her children, who did not deserve to remain haunted by the fears and scars of the past for the rest of their lives.Bilkis and her family left Gujarat earlier this month, her uncle Razzak Mansuri said. "She was in Gujarat until recently, but after SC granted bail to two of the convicts on Oct 28, the family left the state around Nov 2-3. Out of fear, the family periodically changes their place of residence, but stays in Gujarat.This time around they decided to leave Gujarat," he said.Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya were among the 11 men convicted by a special CBI court in Mumbai in 2008 in the case. They were convicted under IPC Section 302 read with Sec 149 for the murder of 14 people, and under Sec 376(2)(e) and 376(2)(g) for gang rape, including the rape of Bilkis Bano, who was pregnant at the time. Bombay HC had upheld this on May 4, 2017.Recalling the horrific events of 2002, Bilkis said she was just 19 years old when her baby daughter, family, home, and trust in humanity were brutally wrenched away.For the past 24 years, she said, she had fought repeatedly for justice, not only for herself but also for women everywhere. She recalled walking from one courtroom to another and being grateful each time she was vindicated and her faith in the idea of justice was restored.An SC bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale granted bail to Joshi and Modhiya, noting that they had been incarcerated for more than 17 years.Bilkis said the order left her feeling that she was losing the very justice she had fought so hard to secure. She said familiar fears had resurfaced and she was scared once again for herself, her family and her children. She also expressed apprehensions about losing faith in the justice system yet again.
Article Summary: After SC order, I'm scared once again for myself & family: Bilkis Bano. Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya were among the 11 men convicted by a special CBI court in 2008 in the case. They were convicted under IPC Section 302 read with Sec 149 for the murder of 14 people, and under Sec 376(2)(e) and 376 (2)(g) for gang rape.

Article Title: Fresh encounter breaks out in J&K's Kulgam
Article Text:
Encounter breaks out between terrorists, security forces in Kulgam

NEW DELHI: A fresh encounter broke out between terrorists and security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on Wednesday morning, officials said. The gunfight involved a joint team of Jammu and Kashmir Police and security forces.The development comes days after a CRPF naka in Akhran came under attack on November 11, leaving three personnel injured. Confirming the fresh encounter, Kashmir Zone Police said in a post on X, "Encounter started with terrorists and Joint party of JKP and SF in Kulgam."Meanwhile, the investigation into the Akhran attack has revealed that the two accused, Umar Nisar Dar and Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Lateef Bhat, had conducted reconnaissance at several locations in Kulgam a day before the incident.CCTV footage shared by Jammu and Kashmir Police showed the duo visiting Mir Baar, Akhran, Hablish and Kilam on November 10. Their movements were captured by cameras installed at multiple locations as they allegedly identified targets and planned attacks against security forces.Also Read| LeT commander Lateef Bhat trapped in J&K's Kulgam encounter, refuses to surrender The following day, November 11, Umar Nisar Dar and Lateef Bhat allegedly carried out an attack on a CRPF naka at Akhran before escaping.Three CRPF personnel were injured when motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on security personnel deployed at the naka.The investigation also uncovered details about Umar Nisar Dar's association with the LeT commander. After Umar went missing, his family approached Police Station Kulgam and lodged a missing report.Further investigation established that Umar had been providing shelter and assistance to Lateef Bhat for the past five to six months. Agencies also found that Umar joined the TRF outfit immediately after the Akhran incident.A subsequent examination of CCTV recordings from November 10 and 11 helped security agencies trace the movements of both men. Their presence was recorded at several locations during the reconnaissance exercise and later as they fled following the attack.The search for the two accused led security forces to Laroo on Monday, where Umar Nisar Dar and Lateef Bhat were intercepted after fleeing the Akhran attack site.An encounter followed, resulting in Umar's death. However, Lateef Bhat remains unaccounted for, with security forces continuing their hunt for the LeT commander.The latest gunfight in Kulgam was reported on Wednesday morning, with a joint team of police and security forces engaging terrorists in the district.
Article Summary: The gunfight involved a joint team of Jammu and Kashmir Police and security forces. The development comes days after a CRPF naka in Akhran came under attack. The investigation into the Akhran attack has revealed that the two accused, Umar Nisar Dar and Lateef Bhat, had conducted reconnaissance at several locations.

Labubu dolls dangling from exclusive designer handbags, squishmallows adorning beds, and your next purchase waiting for you to click “add to cart”. That is the new normal in a society where trends decide what one absolutely needs, and the excuse? #InstagramMadeMeBuyItKananpreet Kaur,19, from Delhi,had purchased an apple watch because it was all the hype. However, the whoop health tracking band is the new “it thing” now, so the watch sits unused. “I had bought it just because everyone around me had one,” she says.Modern marketing and consumer culture often promote the belief that more possessions mean a happier, more content life. Advertisements and social media apps like Instagram, Facebook, and X constantly introduce us to products we never knew we needed. These apps help create the notorious Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), which makes the brain think we are falling behind, ultimately tricking us into frivolous purchases. A 2023 study published in the Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services, titled Fear of Missing Out and Compulsive Buying Behaviour: the Moderating Role of Mindfulnessexamined 569 participants and found that FOMO had a significant effect on compulsive buying.Dubai-resident Ahaana Arora, 19, finds herself with a new craving for tin desserts as they shot to fame on Instagram. “I never anticipated how a dessert tin would find its way to my doorstep every week,” she says.What started with simply trying out a viral sweet treat, has now become an obsession.Overconsumption today goes by a new name: self-care. This includes buying “aesthetic” outfits, the latest Stanley water cup, and stocking up on makeup and skincare products. And although it is pitched as luxurious bubble baths, curated skincare fridges, and expensive workout sets, the focus has shifted from feeling good to looking good for the camera.In today's time where the world is constantly selling you a commodity, recognising the value in each purchase becomes difficult. Something that often begins as a simple purchase leads to a series of transactions you never anticipated, because buying just a foundation is meaningless unless you get the primer for a better grip, a concealer for more coverage, setting powder to avoid creases, and you unquestionably need a setting spray for the look to come together. The growing demand for beauty products in India is also reflected in a 2023 Kantar Worldpanel study which revealed that over 100 million cosmetic products were sold in the country in a span of just six months, generating more than Rs 5000 crores in revenue.Moreover, the fashion industry is responsible for the considerable amount of waste. The total greenhouse gas emissions from the production of textiles clocks in at 1.2 billion tons a year—that’s more than all international flights and maritime ships combined. All the glory goes to the flawlessly engineered algorithm that cleverly blurs the lines between choice and impulse.Today, every purchase has another already waiting in cue. Buying an Iphone leads to icloud, apple music, apple arcade; a dermatologist visit translates to getting a long list of treatments and add ons; join a dating app hoping to meet someone new and wanting more visibility or simply the ability to see who's into you will cost extra; a small purchase from quick delivery apps requires a minimum cart value to avoid several additional fees.Mankeerat Kaur Chaudhary, a 19 year old veterinary student from Amritsar, downloaded the notes app thinking it is free of cost, only to later pay Rs 1200 annually for the premium features.Prisha Kapoor, 20, from Noida, finds it ridiculous how streaming platforms constantly modify their subscriptions plans. Ad free experience, which was once included in the original plan, is now an additional charge away.All these examples point towards a larger phenomenon, called the “diderot effect.’’ The Diderot effect occurs when acquiring a new possession leads to a spiral of consumption.The selling will never end, influencers will continue to stand in front of the camera telling us about their “find of the month”, and the apps will continue to refine their user interfaces to get you hooked. The very notion of ‘authentic self’ is challenged as consumerism permeates our consciousness and molds our perception of what it truly means to be an individual. Perhaps the biggest triumph of modern consumerism is not that our pockets are bleeding dry, but that it makes us believe that we are never quite enough, and how there's always a better version of ourselves waiting for us to swipe the card.
Article Summary: Modern marketing and consumer culture often promote the belief that more possessions mean a happier, more content life. Advertisements and social media apps like Instagram, Facebook, and X constantly introduce us to products we never knew we needed. These apps help create the notorious Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), which makes the brain think we are falling behind, ultimately tricking us into frivolous purchases.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

GTA roleplay streamer Ripoozi, also known as Oozi, was placed in an induced coma after being involved in a serious car crash during TwitchCon weekend. The news was shared by fellow Twitch streamer Deansocool, who explained what happened while speaking during a livestream. According to him, the crash happened when a car driven by an allegedly drunk motorist hit one of the two vehicles carrying members of their group. Several people were taken to the hospital, leaving the GTA roleplay community worried about their recovery.The crash took place during the weekend of TwitchCon San Diego, which was held from November 13 to 15 at the San Diego Convention Center. Deansocool said that members of the group were travelling home in two separate cars when another vehicle hit one of them.He described the other driver as drunk and said that Ripoozi was still in the hospital when he shared the update. The streamer also revealed that other people involved in the crash had suffered injuries. These included a broken foot and a kidney injury.Ripoozi, whose real name has not been shared in the report, has around 64,000 followers on Twitch. He is known for playing Larry Knox on NoPixel, a popular Grand Theft Auto V roleplay server.His character belongs to an in-game crew called BNE, which also includes Cinna's character, Kalita Dub.For those unfamiliar with GTA roleplay, players take on fictional characters and act out different stories inside the game. Ripoozi has built a following through his role as Larry Knox, making the news of his accident especially worrying for fans of the NoPixel community.While Ripoozi remains in the hospital, fellow streamers have stepped in to support his family. Deansocool thanked xQc, Buddha and Cinna for helping fly Ripoozi's mother out to see him.The gesture has received attention from fans because it shows how creators from the GTA roleplay community are coming together during a difficult time.All three streamers have connections to NoPixel. xQc is a co-owner of the server, while Buddha took charge of its daily management in 2023. Cinna is also part of the roleplay community and plays Kalita Dub, a character connected to Ripoozi's in-game crew.The news spread across GTA roleplay communities and the LivestreamFail subreddit, where fans shared messages wishing Ripoozi and the other injured people a quick recovery.For now, Deansocool's livestream remains the main source of the reported details about the accident. No further medical update or confirmed recovery timeline was included in the report.The crash has left many GTA fans concerned about Ripoozi and everyone involved. As the community waits for more news, fans continue to hope that the streamer and the other injured people recover soon.

Several people were taken to the hospital, leaving the GTA community worried.

Article Title: Ed Kelce’s love and sacrifices shaped Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL journey, but his greatest legacy lies in the love that held their family together
Article Text:
Ed Kelce’s love and sacrifices shaped Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL journey, but his greatest legacy lies in the love that held their family together

How Ed Kelce helped Jason and Travis Kelce discover their love for sports

The sacrifices Ed and Donna Kelce made to support their sons

How Ed Kelce and Donna Kelce put their children first despite marriage problems

Ed Kelce never stopped supporting Jason and Travis after their NFL success

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Behind NFL stars Jason and Travis Kelce ’s success is a father who spent years making sure they had the support to follow their dreams. Ed Kelce coached them, encouraged their love for sports and made personal sacrifices to give them better opportunities. Even when his marriage with Donna Kelce faced difficulties, he continued putting his sons first. His journey shows how much a parent’s support can matter in a child’s life.Ed Kelce grew up in Cleveland, Ohio, where he developed an interest in football and baseball. Having played both sports himself, he understood how much they could teach children. When Jason and Travis were young, he wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path.He started getting involved when the boys were very little. Ed coached Travis in T-ball and Jason in coach-pitch baseball. He also spent time playing with them in the front yard and created space in the family garage where they could practise.One of his favourite memories goes back to when Jason was still a toddler. His son would roll a ball towards him on the living-room floor, and Ed would roll it back. It was a simple activity, but it became one of their earliest shared memories.Years later, while appearing on the brothers’ New Heights podcast, Ed explained how he viewed his responsibility as a father.“My job is to help you find a passion, and then feed that passion. Whatever you want to do, I’m there.”He wanted both boys to discover what they enjoyed and then work towards becoming better at it. He also believed that talent needed to be supported by hard work. Rather than always placing them in situations where they could easily succeed, he encouraged them to compete and learn from more difficult experiences.That approach helped Jason and Travis develop their interest in football. Both eventually attended the University of Cincinnati, where they played college football before entering the NFL.Raising two children with serious sporting ambitions required time, money and a lot of planning. Jason and Travis played different sports and had busy schedules, so their parents had to manage practices, competitions, travel and equipment costs.Ed worked in the steel industry before moving into sales, while Donna built her career in banking. Both had professional responsibilities, but they made sure their sons received the support they needed.The financial side was not always easy. The family had to plan its spending around the boys’ sporting activities, including equipment, travel and other expenses. Ed and Donna had to make choices to ensure both children could take part in the activities they enjoyed.They also divided their parenting responsibilities carefully. Donna explained on New Heights that they worked as a team. When one parent travelled with Jason for a game, the other stayed home with Travis. This allowed both boys to receive attention and support, even when their schedules clashed.Donna described their arrangement as being “like a tag team with you two.”It was not always possible for both parents to attend every event, but they made sure someone was there. Their priority was to give Jason and Travis equal opportunities rather than allowing one child’s sporting commitments to take over family life.Neither Ed nor Donna knew that their sons would eventually become NFL stars. They were simply making sure the boys had the chance to explore their interests and work towards their goals.While Ed and Donna were busy raising their sons, their own marriage was going through a difficult period. The couple had been married for nearly 25 years, but their relationship was not always happy.Travis spoke about this in the Prime Video documentary Kelce. He remembered noticing during childhood that his parents did not share a bedroom. As he reached middle school, he began to understand that their marriage was struggling.Despite their personal problems, Ed and Donna continued raising their sons together. They knew that separating while Jason and Travis were still studying and playing sports would make an already busy family life more difficult.Ed explained their decision in the documentary, saying, “If we had split as we probably both would have preferred, that would have been a nightmare with the logistics, getting kids where they had to be and providing all the support.”His words give an idea of the practical challenges they were trying to avoid. They had to manage school, sports, travel and other family responsibilities, and both understood how much their sons depended on them.Their marriage eventually ended in divorce after Jason and Travis had graduated from college. However, their separation did not end their responsibilities as parents. They continued to support their sons and remained connected as a family.Donna has also spoken warmly about Ed and their years together, making it clear that she does not regret the family they built.Ed’s involvement did not end when his sons left home for college. When Jason joined the Philadelphia Eagles and Travis became a star with the Kansas City Chiefs, he continued attending games and following their careers.Supporting both sons became more challenging once they started playing for different NFL teams. Their games were often held in different cities, making it difficult for Ed and Donna to be present at every match. They continued dividing their time so both brothers could receive support.One of the most memorable moments came during Super Bowl LVII in February 2023, when Jason’s Eagles faced Travis’s Chiefs. It was an unusual situation for the family because one son would celebrate winning the championship while the other would have to deal with defeat.Ed understood how difficult that could be. Before the game, he explained that he wanted to be with whichever son lost.“Somebody’s gonna feel pretty crummy and I wanna be with him-initially.”He also joked that he had already won because both his sons had reached the Super Bowl.The game ended with Travis and the Chiefs defeating Jason and the Eagles 38-35. Ed and Donna celebrated with Travis but also had to share the difficult moment with Jason.For Ed, the journey was about much more than watching his sons become famous football players. He had been there when they first started playing sports, helped them through their childhood and continued supporting them when their careers reached the highest level.His story is a reminder that behind many successful athletes are parents who make sacrifices without knowing where their children’s dreams will eventually lead.
Article Summary: Ed Kelce coached Jason and Travis Kelce when they were young. He wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path. Ed and Donna Kelce made sacrifices to give their sons better opportunities. Even when their marriage was going through difficulties, he continued putting his sons first.

Article Title: A coconut worth less than 100 rupees just sold for Rs 2.55 lakh at a Tamil Nadu temple, and the reason behind it has devotees talking
Article Text:
Devotees bid big for a sacred coconut blessed at Murugan’s wedding.

Why this coconut was so special

Brings prosperity

Helps unmarried family members find partners

Blesses childless couples with children

A tradition where the price keeps climbing

The festival behind the frenzy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MADURAI: A coconut that would normally cost a few dozen rupees just sold for Rs 2.55 lakh. The bidding war took place at the Subramaniya Swamy temple in Bodinayakanur, Theni district in Tamil Nadu on Monday.The auction opened at just Rs 11,000, but devotees kept pushing the price higher.One Gunasekaran from Bodinayakanur took his bid to Rs 2.45 lakh. Then Renuka from Chellampatti near Madurai came back with an offer Rs 10,000 higher. After more than 30 minutes of bidding, she walked away as the winner.Temple authorities honoured Renuka’s family with garlands and handed over the prized offering.This was no ordinary coconut. It had been used during the celestial wedding of Lord Murugan with Valli and Deivanai at the temple in Theni district, and the sacred thirumangalyam (marriage pendant) was placed around it.Devotees believe that keeping the coconut at home and worshipping it:The auction followed Monday’s Thirukalyanam, held as part of the Kanda Sashti festival that began on Nov 10 across Tamil Nadu.It is an annual tradition at the temple, and the competition is getting more expensive. Last year’s coconut fetched Rs 2 lakh, while a ceremonial coconut auctioned during an earlier Uthira festival went for Rs 3.03 lakh.Kanda Sashti is a six-day festival, and its climax is the “Soorasamharam” ritual.On Sunday, lakhs of devotees, chanting hymns and observing strict fasts, thronged Lord Murugan temples across Tamil Nadu to witness it.The festival marks the mythological battle in which Lord Murugan, armed with the “Vel” (spear) gifted by his mother Goddess Parvati, defeated the demon king Surapadman. It celebrates the victory of light over evil and is observed with great fervour across the state, especially at the “Arupadaiveedu”, the six abodes of the deity.The ritual draws its largest audience at Tiruchendur, where the battle between Murugan and the demon armies of Surapadman is believed to have taken place on the seashore.For many, the enactment is deeply emotional. Sushmitha, a devotee from Chennai who was observing the fast for the third year in a row, said, “When the deity comes forward during the Soorasamharam, tears just roll down your eyes, and it gives you goosebumps.”Observed in the Tamil month of Aipasi, Soorasamharam, also called Suranporu, marks the culmination of the Sashti fast. The six-day observances concluded with the Thirukalyanam of Lord Murugan on Monday.
Article Summary: The auction opened at just Rs 11,000, but devotees kept pushing the price higher. The auction followed Monday’s Thirukalyanam, held as part of the Kanda Sashti festival. The festival marks the mythological battle in which Lord Murugan defeated the demon king Surapadman.

Article Title: Will Austin Reaves play tonight against the Hornets? Lakers get another setback as JJ Redick faces a growing injury concern
Article Text:
Austin Reaves. Image via: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images

Is Austin Reaves playing tonight against the Hornets?

Kessler’s leg soreness and the Lakers’ lineup

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Austin Reaves will learn Wednesday morning whether his bruised left heel is ready for the Utah Jazz. Lakers coach JJ Redick said the guard is scheduled to work out on the court that morning, and the result will decide the call for the game. The bruise has already forced Reaves out of two straight games. Walker Kessler also sat Tuesday against Charlotte with a sore lower leg, though Redick does not see a serious problem there. The Jazz visit comes one night after the Hornets game, with both on the home floor.Austin Reaves is ruled out for the Los Angeles Lakers' game against the Charlotte Hornets. Reaves hurt the heel last week in Milwaukee, a 123-112 Lakers win, then missed the 131-123 win over Phoenix on Sunday. Reaves was ruled out again for Tuesday’s game against the struggling Hornets (4-9), so Wednesday would make it three in a row.Redick said the plan is for Reaves to get on the court Wednesday morning “to see how he feels,” as relayed by reporter Daniel Starkand. No timeline came with the update beyond that workout.Quentin Grimes has started in the guard’s place for both absences. Reaves is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds and 4.7 assists across 12 appearances, and this is the first season Reaves has been the second option on an NBA team.Role players such as Ziaire Williams and Jake LaRavia have stepped up when Reaves or Luka Doncic sat. Missed games could still cost Reaves in All-Star talk, with Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in a deep Western guard pool.Kessler sat out Tuesday with right lower leg soreness. Redick called it a precaution and expects the center back Wednesday. It was the first game Kessler has missed this season, and he appeared in just six games for Utah last year.Kessler’s rim protection and lob finishing have made him a key piece of the rotation. Sandro Mamukelashvili is the team’s best bench big, and Jarred Vanderbilt could slide to center if Redick goes small. The back end of the rotation is harder to read. Williams and Adou Thiero were the expected bench wings, with rookie Cameron Carr and Jaden Hardy also possible.Grimes showed up on Tuesday’s injury report with an available tag. The projected starters for that game were Doncic, Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, LaRavia and Mamukelashvili. Doncic and Thybulle have started every game they have played, and LaRavia has taken the forward spot from Williams. Article Title: A 95-year-old British widow faces legal costs exceeding £1 million after a 10-year fence dispute over about 45 square metres of land, despite winning damages for trespass; a judge has now dismissed he
Article Text:
(AI Image)

A costly decade-long legal feud

Judge describes result as a 'score draw'

High Court appeal dismissed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 95-year-old British widow is facing legal bills of more than £1 million after spending a decade fighting her neighbours over a garden fence. The High Court has rejected an appeal by Margaret Kinnear against a ruling that she must pay her own legal costs in the dispute. This is despite her having successfully won a trespass claim against the couple living next door. The dispute involved a boundary line in the wealthy village of Sissinghurst, near Tunbridge Wells in Kent. At the centre of the case was a narrow strip of land measuring around 45 square metres. A judge described the area as being of "extremely limited, if any, usable or other value."Neighbours Neil and Fiona Morgan put up a new fence in late 2015, replacing an existing fence along the boundary of Mrs Kinnear's property. According to court reports, the Morgans first placed fence posts on Mrs Kinnear's land without asking her. They later removed the posts and put up a second fence. This was followed by a temporary fence that extended further onto her property. Finally, they installed a permanent fence with concrete posts in January 2016. This became known as the "third fence." The legal battle began when the Morgans sued Mrs Kinnear for damages, claiming she had destroyed their second fence.Mrs Kinnear filed a counterclaim, accusing the couple of trespassing by putting up the fences. She also asked the court to declare that the true boundary ran along a line of hedges and trees.The case went to trial at Maidstone County Court in 2021. Recorder John Dagnall dismissed the Morgans' claim and ruled that they had trespassed by building the fences. He awarded Mrs Kinnear nominal damages of £2,600. However, the judge also rejected her request to have the third fence removed. Instead, he declared that the fence would mark the new boundary and awarded her £3,250 in damages instead of ordering its removal through an injunction.At a later hearing about legal costs in 2024, Recorder Dagnall ruled that both sides should pay their own legal bills. He effectively described the outcome as a "score draw." This left Mrs Kinnear responsible for her entire legal bill, which was reported to exceed £1 million. The Morgans had also faced substantial legal expenses. However, they represented themselves for much of the court battle, meaning their overall costs were lower. Mrs Kinnear appealed against the decision on legal costs, arguing that she had been the real winner of the case. Her lawyers said Neil Morgan's "egregious" and "disgraceful" behaviour during the proceedings should have led the court to order the Morgans to pay her legal expenses.The appeal was heard in the High Court last week by Mr Justice Tappin. Mrs Kinnear's barrister presented examples of personal insults used by Mr Morgan in court documents and communications. These included attacks on opposing lawyers, their staff and judges. In one email, he reportedly called a junior solicitor a "lying hypocritical devious arse." In a letter sent to the court, he described a Deputy District Judge as "moronic and genuinely not fit to judge vegetables at a village fete. "Delivering his judgment yesterday, Mr Justice Tappin agreed that Mr Morgan's language was "deplorable and unacceptable." However, he found no reason to overturn the original judge's decision. He agreed that Recorder Dagnall had been entitled to conclude that Mr Morgan's behaviour did not justify changing the order on legal costs. The High Court judge also supported the original decision to consider Mrs Kinnear's failure to win her main argument about the location of the property boundary.Although she had won her trespass claim, she had not secured the outcome she wanted on the boundary itself.Mr Justice Tappin also expressed regret about the huge amount of time and money spent on the dispute. Reporting on the judgment, The Independent quoted Mr Justice Tappin as saying that the argument over the "sliver of grass, tree and scrub... of extremely limited, if any, usable or other value" had led to an "expenditure of time, cost and energy wholly out of proportion to the financial value of the area of land in dispute. " The High Court's decision means that the 95-year-old widow must pay her own legal costs, which exceed £1 million, bringing another setback in her decade-long dispute with her neighbours.
Article Summary: Margaret Kinnear, 95, has spent a decade fighting her neighbours over a garden fence. The High Court has rejected an appeal against a ruling that she must pay her own legal costs in the dispute. This is despite her having successfully won a trespass claim against the couple living next door.

Article Title: Former WWE star Dana Brooke has big family news after overcoming personal heartbreak and health challenges
Article Text:
Dana Brooke. Image via: WWE

What did Dana Brooke go through before this pregnancy news?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

TNA contract status and a possible return to the ring

Former WWE star Dana Brooke is 32 weeks pregnant with a baby boy. The wrestler, who now competes as Ash By Elegance, shared the news on TMZ’s Inside The Ring and said her due date is January 11, 2027. Brooke reached this point after a miscarriage last year, an ICU stay in February and a Crohn’s disease diagnosis in May. Doctors still classify the pregnancy as high-risk. She says she feels better than ever anyway. The birth is planned as a C-section, and her son already has a name: Kairos.Brooke first became pregnant in August 2025, which led to her retirement announcement from TNA. Two months later she had a miscarriage. In February 2026, severe stomach pain and internal bleeding put her in the ICU. She needed three blood transfusions and was moved between three hospitals while doctors hunted for a cause.The answer came on May 6, when she was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease. It is a lifelong autoimmune condition, and Brooke now takes monthly infusions and a monthly injection. She had never been ill in her life, so the news came out of nowhere.She was also told to step back from wrestling because of inflammation in her intestines and stomach, and she admits she took it badly.At the end of May, she found out she was pregnant again. Brooke says the miscarriage taught her to wait. She had told her work, friends and parents the first time and was about to announce it publicly when everything fell apart. This time she told no one, not work, family or friends, until she passed the halfway mark. A gender reveal party followed.Brooke says “he has been a blessing, he’s been a miracle.” Her doctors told her pregnancy can steer Crohn’s toward remission, and she says that is what happened. She has had no flare-ups since the early stages, and her 32-week scan showed a thriving baby.Brooke’s TNA contract expires at the end of December, and the company has left the door open for a return. She announced her retirement from TNA after that first pregnancy in 2025, but the promotion has not shut her out.She has the résumé to back a comeback. Brooke joined NXT in 2013 after competing in fitness events, and in 2015 she became the first WWE Superstar to enter the Fitness International competition at the Arnold Sports Festival. She later won the 24/7 Championship multiple times. In TNA, she captured the Knockouts title.Brooke hopes to step back into the ring one day and show her son just how tough his mom is. For now, the focus is a healthy delivery in January, with a team of doctors working with her through a high-risk pregnancy.

Article Title: Magnus Carlsen didn't show up for fast classical chess: Who is at fault?
Article Text:
Magnus Carlsen didn't show up for fast classical chess against Bibisara Assaubayeva

Magnus Carlsen and Bibisara Assaubayeva during the players' group photoshoot (Photo by Total Chess)

What happened?

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with Magnus Carlsen's decision to forfeit the final game? Yes, it was a smart choice. No, it was unsportsmanlike. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

What the rules say

Magnus Carlsen vs Bibisara Assaubayeva (Photo by Michal Walusza for Total Chess)

What the organisers say

The argument of morality

What the players say

Magnus Carlsen vs Bibisara Assaubayeva (Photo by Maria Emelianova for Total Chess)

What it leaves the organisers with

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: During the players' group photoshoot before the Total Chess Pilot event in Budapest, Hungary, five-time world champion and current World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen was one of the last to arrive, climbing a couple of stairs to sneak into the group photo from the back and finding his place beside Kazakh Grandmaster Bibisara Assaubayeva.Soon, cutouts and clips of the two standing together started doing the rounds, captioned along the lines of "no weak characters" and "imagine the number of World Championships they share between them" — 23 in total, Carlsen alone accounting for 20.Little did anyone know that both would end up sitting across the board in a match to decide 17th-21st place in this pilot event, and that one of them choosing not to show up for the day's final game would put them at the centre of a heated debate Carlsen had already sealed the match before a single Fast Classical move was played. He beat Assaubayeva 3-0 in Blitz with one draw, and 2-0 in Rapid, putting the score at 11.5-0.5. The match was decided, regardless of what happened next.Before the Fast Classical round began, Carlsen walked out of the playing hall. Asked why by Norwegian media outlet TV2, he said, "There will be no classical game as I understood, the match is over.The only consequence of not showing up is that you will lose a totally useless game. I think that if you play a World Championship and it counts for points and such, I can understand. But this is not a show tournament. If the match is done, it's done. In the end, if you play games after, it shall not be rated because it's always been like that. And if they want to do things differently here... yeah. This is my decision on this topic."After the mandatory 15-minute default period, Assaubayeva walked out too, awarded the win on forfeit. Day 1 of the semifinal closed 11.5-8.5 in Carlsen's favour. The game, which was supposed to count towards FIDE ratings, went unplayed and therefore had no impact on either player's classical rating.Chief arbiter Anastasia Sorokina, speaking to ChessBase India at the venue, confirmed that any further penalties for the forfeit would be at the organisers' discretion."The result is minus-plus because Magnus didn't appear for the game. From our perspective as arbiters, there are no extra penalties for this, except the game is minus-plus, of course," she said."There is a point about the possible fees that organisers could apply, but it's not directly connected to the game. So it depends on the situation, organisers will decide."Under FIDE's regulations, forfeited games don't count toward classical ratings, which is precisely what made the decision rational for Carlsen.He'd had a torn group stage in the Fast Classical format, failing to win any of his 10 games, drawing nine and losing one to Armenia's Haik Martirosyan, a run that cost him 21.8 Elo points and pushed his live rating down to 2801.2, uncomfortably close to Hikaru Nakamura and Fabiano Caruana overtaking him as World No. 1.A draw against Assaubayeva would have cost him 3.5 more rating points, a defeat 8.5. By forfeiting, he avoided both, since an unplayed game carries no rating consequence at all. Total Chess founder and CEO Kjell Madland also shared his view on the situation."He (Carlsen) was there and discussed it with the arbiter team. The system is to win the day, and he had already won enough points to win the day. So then he didn't want to play the last game, and he didn't need to do it," he told ChessBase India.On whether Assaubayeva was informed beforehand, he replied, "No, because he could play if he wanted to play. We of course didn't discuss this with Bibisara before, that was not necessary."Pressed on whether the rules might change after this forfeit, Madland added, "The rules are the same for everyone. We can't do any differences between the players. It's the same for everyone. So if that happens tomorrow with someone else, it happened."Calling Budapest "an important learning exercise" ahead of the tour's inaugural edition in March 2027, the organisers stressed they weren't approaching the feedback "with a predetermined view that the rules need to change".Whatever the rules allowed, there was a simpler courtesy Carlsen could have extended and chose not to. By his own account, and the organisers’, he had already decided against playing and discussed the matter with the arbiter team before the round began. The decision, therefore, had been made well before Assaubayeva took her seat at the board.However, with no prior communication, Assaubayeva was left waiting through the full 15-minute default period for an opponent who had no intention of showing up.The rulebook may have little to say about such omissions, governing forfeits rather than the courtesy of forewarning, but it is difficult to separate the question of sportsmanship from the technicalities of the regulations.A simple two-line message through the arbiters would have cost Carlsen nothing and spared Assaubayeva an entirely unnecessary wait.That it never came makes this less a question of what the rules required and more one of the basic consideration an opponent deserves.American Grandmaster Hans Niemann took to social media to voice his concerns. "It was already known that we have to play all the games, we talked about it in the technical meeting," he wrote on X."It's incredibly disappointing to see continued favouritism towards one player. Let's not forget the jeans, and 'Co World Champion' saga. All rules must be applied equally, regardless of the player."Alireza Firouzja noted the same technical meeting had addressed it directly, though Norwegian outlet TV2 reported Carlsen wasn't present for that meeting.Wesley So, on the other hand, saw little wrong with the logic."I think Magnus' decision was understandable. He already won the match, and if he lost to Bibi, he loses 9 points and the No. 1 spot. I don't see yet why Magnus was wrong," he wrote on X.Every answer in this saga is technically correct, and that's precisely the problem. The rules allowed it, the arbiters applied them without penalty, and Carlsen broke no regulation in walking out.But a pilot event exists to surface exactly this kind of gap, between what the rulebook permits and what the field considers fair, before it hardens into precedent.India's Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa, who lost 19.3 rating points of his own in this pilot event, raised a broader gripe about dead-rubber games."It doesn't matter if you finish sixth in the group stage, you still have to play, which is kind of, honestly, sad," he said in an interview with Total Chess. "By that point the player has already started thinking about the next tournament, but he still has to play a game."With the inaugural Total Chess World Championship Tour arriving in March 2027, the organisation now has a concrete decision to make: whether a dead-rubber game, once a match is mathematically settled, should exist at all, or whether, if it does, every player is held to showing up regardless of stakes.Leaving that ambiguous is what turned one player's rational choice into a credibility question for the format itself.It also calls for a separate conversation about the structure of a tournament like this, with some players seemingly unhappy with the number of games scheduled each day across the different formats."I just felt envious that you can solve the sports part in Rapid and Blitz portion and then have a nice evening without chess, which is understandable because we have five days in a row with two rounds every day," Russian Grandmaster Ian Nepomniachtchi told ChessBase India. "Of course, there was a rest day, but it was overall a bit tiring."
Article Summary: Magnus Carlsen didn't show up for fast classical chess against Bibisara Assaubayeva. Carlsen had already sealed the match before a single Fast Classical move was played. The game, which was supposed to count towards FIDE ratings, went unplayed and had no impact on either player's classical rating.

Article Title: Stephen Curry's biggest smile may have come from watching son Cannon deliver a flawless 10-point performance

How did Canon Curry put together his perfect shooting performance?

Stephen Curry's family outings offer a glimpse beyond basketball

Stephen Curry has spent much of his NBA career making difficult shots look routine. But his latest memorable basketball moment had little to do with the Warriors or another milestone in his own career. The 38-year-old guard watched his eight-year-old son, Canon Curry, put together a perfect shooting performance during an elementary school game. Canon finished with 10 points, converting all five of his attempts. For Stephen, watching from the crowd offered a different kind of satisfaction. His son was enjoying the game on his own terms, even as the Curry family name brought extra attention to the performance.Canon's 10-point outing stood out because he did not miss a single attempt. Going 5-for-5 is an impressive return for any player, but it carries an added connection when the player watching from the sidelines is one of basketball's greatest shooters.Stephen has often shared small stories about his son's personality around the game. During a 2022 appearance on Dubs Talk, the Warriors star recalled how Canon was already developing his own approach to shooting rather than simply following instructions from his father.Curry explained that his young son was not always interested in copying his advice. Canon's response was direct: "No, this is how I'm doing it."Those moments offer a glimpse of a child who enjoys basketball but is also comfortable doing things his own way. His latest performance adds another chapter to that story. However, one elementary school game is not a measure of what his future in basketball will look like. For now, the perfect shooting record is enough to celebrate.Stephen's presence at Canon's game fits into a pattern of making time for his children outside his demanding NBA schedule. Earlier in November, he took Canon and his older daughter Riley to Levi's Stadium to watch the San Francisco 49ers face the Las Vegas Raiders.The family watched from a suite as San Francisco secured a 38-17 victory. Stephen also spent time with Bay Area rapper E-40 during the outing.Canon has also shared moments with his father's former Warriors teammate Klay Thompson. Earlier this month, he joined Stephen in greeting Thompson before the Miami Heat's visit to Chase Center. Thompson spent 13 seasons in Golden State, winning four championships alongside Curry.These appearances show how Stephen includes his children in different parts of his life, whether it is an NFL afternoon or a reunion with a former teammate.

Article Title: 'Will miss walking out with this rockstar': Travis Head's emotional message for Abhishek Sharma
Article Text:

Why Travis Head is skipping IPL 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The explosive opening partnership between Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma will not be seen in IPL 2027. Head has decided to skip the next season to focus on his international commitments and spend more time with his family, bringing an end to one of the most exciting opening combinations in the tournament.Sunrisers Hyderabad released the Australian batter ahead of the upcoming season. Following the development, Abhishek shared an emotional message for his opening partner on social media on Tuesday.Head also took to social media and posted a series of pictures with Abhishek, remembering their time together at Sunrisers Hyderabad."Will miss walking out with this rockstar," Head wrote.Abhishek responded with a short but heartfelt message for the Australian."Thank you Heady for everything," read his reply.Head and Abhishek formed a destructive opening pair for Sunrisers Hyderabad, putting opposition bowlers under pressure from the start.In 43 appearances for SRH, Head scored 1,351 runs at an average of 32.95 and an impressive strike rate of 176.14. However, his partnership with Abhishek became one of the biggest highlights of his time with the franchise.The duo scored 1,892 runs in 42 innings together at an average of 46.14.They put together six century partnerships and nine stands of at least 50 runs.Only Shikhar Dhawan and David Warner have scored more runs as an opening pair for SRH. However, Head and Abhishek hold a special record. Their scoring rate of 12.46 runs per over is the highest in IPL history among partnerships that have scored at least 1,000 runs.With Head unavailable, SRH will now have to look for a new opening partner for Abhishek at the IPL 2027 auction, scheduled to take place on December 16.Head explained that he wanted to focus on his international career while also giving more time to his family. The Australian said leaving SRH was a difficult decision after three memorable seasons with the franchise."After three incredible years with Sunrisers Hyderabad, I want to take a moment to say a heartfelt thank you to everyone who has been part of the journey," Head was quoted in a social media post shared by the franchise."This has been an extremely difficult decision, but with my ongoing international ambitions and the importance of finding a better work-life balance for my family, I feel it's the right one at this stage of my career.""I'm extremely proud of what we've achieved together and will always look back on my time at Sunrisers Hyderabad with great memories and appreciation," the left-handed batter said.
Article Summary: Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma will not be seen in IPL 2027. Head has decided to skip the next season to focus on his international commitments and spend more time with his family. Sharma shared an emotional message for his opening partner on social media.
