Article Title: No Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, no problem! Bihar pull off thrilling two-wicket win over Delhi in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
Article Text:
Wicketkeeper-batter Ayush Loharuka led the charge with a quick 50 off 22 balls (Image credit: X)

Yash Dhull 's century powers Delhi to 224

Loharuka, Bipin give Bihar a flying start

Mayank, Prashant keep their nerve in tense finish

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bihar showed they can win without their star batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, pulling off a thrilling two-wicket victory over Delhi in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at the Daly College Ground in Indore.Chasing a massive target of 225, Bihar reached 227 for eight in 19.5 overs, with Mayank Kumar and Prashant Singh holding their nerve in the final overs to take the team across the line.Sooryavanshi was missing from the Bihar side as he is set to join the India A squad for the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, which begins in Doha on November 20. India A will open their campaign against Nepal.After being asked to bat, Delhi posted a huge total of 224 for five in their 20 overs, thanks to a brilliant century from Yash Dhull.Dhull smashed 125 off just 59 balls, hitting 16 fours and seven sixes. He dominated the innings and shared a 126-run partnership with Tejasvi Dahiya, who scored 51 off 25 balls.Dahiya struck four fours and four sixes as Delhi finished with a run rate of 11.2.Raghuvendra Pratap Singh was Bihar's most successful bowler, picking up three wickets for 44 runs. Prashant Singh and Suraj Kashyap took one wicket each.Bihar began their chase aggressively, scoring 96 runs in the first six overs.Wicketkeeper-batter Ayush Loharuka led the charge with a quick 50 off 22 balls, including seven fours and three sixes. He added 103 runs with Bipin Saurabh for the second wicket.Bipin also played an attacking knock, scoring 49 off just 19 balls with three fours and five sixes. Their partnership put Bihar in a strong position in the chase.However, Delhi fought back through their spinners. Digvesh Singh Rathi picked up three wickets for 47 runs, while Suyash Sharma and Keshav Dabas claimed one wicket each.Bihar lost wickets at regular intervals after the strong start and slipped to 189 for eight in the 17th over. With 36 runs still needed from the final three overs, the match was in the balance.Mayank Kumar and Prashant Singh then turned the game around with an important unbeaten partnership.Mayank provided the late fireworks, hitting three sixes in his unbeaten 24 off 13 balls. Prashant remained not out on 13 off eight deliveries, hitting two fours.The pair took 19 runs off the 18th over bowled by Keshav Dabas, including two sixes from Mayank. They then collected five runs in the 19th over before Prashant struck a boundary off Nitish Rana in the final over to seal the win with one ball remaining.Bihar finished on 227 for eight in 19.5 overs to register a memorable two-wicket victory.
Article Summary: Bihar beat Delhi by two wickets in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Yash Dhull hit 125 as Delhi posted 224 for five in their 20 overs. Bihar reached 227 for eight in 19.5 overs, with Mayank Kumar and Prashant Singh holding their nerve in the final overs.

Article Title: ‘Will marry you after divorce’: 41-year-old foreign student booked for raping woman
Article Text:
A 34-year-old woman has reported that a 41-year-old Gambian national sexually exploited her under the pretext of marriage.

BHOPAL: A 34-year-old woman has accused a 41-year-old Gambian national, who came to India to study, of repeatedly sexually exploiting her on the pretext of marriage. She alleged that he promised to marry her after she obtained a divorce from her husband. She approached police on Monday after learning that he was allegedly involved with another woman in Bhopal.According to police, the woman met the accused around a year ago when he frequently visited the fast-food stall she ran with her husband in Kolar. Their acquaintance gradually developed into friendship. The accused is a student at a private university and lives with other students in Danish Kunj.The woman told police that she had filed for divorce following marital disputes. The accused allegedly assured her that he would marry her once the divorce was finalised. In February 2026, when her husband was away, he allegedly visited her home and established physical relations with her on that assurance. She claimed he continued to do so repeatedly.She further alleged that she learnt a few days before filing the complaint that he was in a relationship with another woman. On November 14, she went to his house with her brother to confront him. The accused allegedly pushed and manhandled her, prompting her brother to intervene.The woman later informed her husband and approached police. Kolar police registered a case of rape and assault against the accused and started an investigation.
Article Summary: A Gambian national, who came to India to study, allegedly sexually exploited a 34-year-old woman. She alleged that he promised to marry her after she obtained a divorce from her husband. Kolar police registered a case of rape and assault against the accused and started an investigation.

Article Title: Dodged CCTV at stations, rode 2,000 km across 4 states on bike: How Bengaluru murder accused was nabbed in Bihar
Article Text:
Amit Kumar Dubey became a prime suspect in the murder of advocate Manjunath in Whitefield

The cross-country escape

His escape route spanned roughly five to six days

Hyderabad (around 575 km from Bengaluru): Dubey’s first major halt, where he sold one of his mobile handsets at a throwaway price to raise cash and spent the night sleeping at a railway station.

Nagpur (around 500 km from Hyderabad): After riding north from Telangana into Maharashtra, he rested overnight at a local bus stand.

Nagpur to Varanasi –Around 730 km.

Varanasi to Bihar (around 230 km): Crossing into Uttar Pradesh and eventually Bihar, he avoided hotels, opting instead to pay Rs 200–300 a night for a rope cot (charpai) at roadside dhabas.

Upon reaching Patna district, Dubey sought shelter with a distant maternal relative in Nanauri. Keeping a low profile, he blended into rural life by taking up work as an agricultural labourer on his relative’s farm for Rs 400 a day.

How police cracked the trail

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





BENGALURU: Desperate to evade the dragnet of highway and transit surveillance, a suspect in last month’s sensational murder of a Whitefield advocate travelled at least 2,000 km across four states on a commuter motorcycle, only to be tracked down working as a daily-wage farmhand in a remote Bihar village.Amit Kumar Dubey, one of the two prime suspects accused of gunning down advocate Manjunath in Whitefield last month, was arrested last Friday by a police team in Nanauri village, located in the Dhanarua block of Patna district.When investigators finally caught up with him and asked why he had opted for an exhausting five-to-six-day road journey on a Hero Honda Splendor instead of taking public transport, Dubey reportedly gave a straightforward answer: “I was aware that there are CCTV cameras at bus stands and railway stations, and police would easily catch me.”Deputy commissioner of police, Whitefeild, Saidulu Adavat told TOI that it was a challenging job."He was continuously riding on motorbike and we did not have CCTV footages after Varanasi : that really become difficult also he was not regulatory using mobile phone. Even while working as a daily wage worker changed his name," Adavat said.Probe revealed that immediately after the crime, Dubey packed a single backpack with clothes, a charger, and electronic gadgets.Wearing a jacket and a full-face helmet to conceal his identity, he set off northwards, riding from daybreak until nightfall and surviving on meals at roadside eateries.Despite his attempts to evade surveillance, Dubey’s solo journey was captured by several highway CCTV cameras along the Bengaluru–Hyderabad–Nagpur corridor. The trail briefly went cold beyond Nagpur, where surveillance infrastructure along the highway was sparse. However, investigators secured a crucial breakthrough when footage from a fuel station on the outskirts of Varanasi confirmed that he was heading towards Bihar.Meanwhile, an analysis of Dubey’s past call detail records (CDRs) revealed that he was in frequent contact with his grandmother, who lives in Nanauri. Suspecting that he might eventually return to his native village, police had raided the area shortly after the murder but returned empty-handed.Keeping the village under discreet surveillance, a team of officers in plain clothes finally moved in last Friday. They tracked Dubey to the agricultural fields where he was working and apprehended him before he could flee.Police are still searching for the prime suspect, Pavan , who allegedly shot the advocate dead.
Article Summary: Amit Kumar Dubey, one of the two prime suspects accused of gunning down advocate Manjunath in Whitefield last month, was arrested last Friday by a police team in Nanauri village. Dubey travelled at least 2,000 km across four states on a commuter motorcycle. He was tracked down working as a daily-wage farmhand in a remote Bihar village.

Article Title: Jaipur cafe owner beaten with rods on way home dies after 11 days; 3 held
Article Text:
Mayank Gopaliya, the cafe owner, was attacked on November 5 while walking home after closing his shop

JAIPUR: A cafe owner who was brutally assaulted near his shop in Vaishali Nagar on Nov 5 died in hospital late Monday night, 11 days after the attack. Police have arrested three men for the assault, which allegedly stemmed from the owner’s objection to a female employee’s friend frequenting the cafe.Mayank Gopaliya, who ran a bakery and cafe on Vaishali Marg and lived in Vaishali Nagar, was attacked around 9:45 pm while walking home after closing his cafe. Two men allegedly ran towards him from behind and repeatedly struck him with sticks and rods. He collapsed after being hit on the head.The attackers fled with their associates, who were waiting on a motorcycle and a scooter, after assuming Gopaliya was dead. He suffered serious head injuries and underwent surgery. He died during treatment at a private hospital late Monday night. His body was shifted to Jaipuria Hospital mortuary for post-mortem.Police have arrested Mohammad Shahrukh, Akman and Mohammad Rashid alias Altamash in connection with the attack. Investigators said Shahrukh often visited the cafe to meet a woman employee. Mayank had objected to this, following which Shahrukh allegedly threatened to kill him.A quarrel took place between them on Nov 5. That night, Shahrukh allegedly joined his associates in attacking Gopaliya.
Article Summary: Mayank Gopaliya was attacked on November 5 while walking home after closing his shop. He suffered serious head injuries and underwent surgery. Police have arrested Mohammad Shahrukh, Akman and Mohammad Rashid alias Altamash in connection with the attack.

Article Title: Married UP sub-inspector dies by suicide; woman accused of blackmail arrested for abetment
Article Text:

VARANASI: A 2023-batch police sub-inspector, Sandeep Kumar , 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district.Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him.Ballia SP Iraj Raja on Sunday said that following collection of evidences and lodging of a complaint by Kumar's wife the accused woman Roli Gond was arrested from an orchard near the railway station on the charges of abetment of suicide.Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.Earlier, the incident came to light when a train’s loco pilot informed the Chitbaragaon station master through a memo that someone had jumped before his moving train to commit suicide.On being alerted by railway officials Chitbadagaon police and GRP reached the spot, where Kumar's motorbike and mobile phone were found lying near the railway track while his mutilated body was detected on tracks.On getting information Raja, ASP South Sanjay Verma, CO Akshay Kumar and railway police officials also reached there while forensic team was engaged to collect evidence from the railway track area.Kumar, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar, was married and had a six-month-old child. He had been posted at Chitbaragaon police station for past 11 months.He was transferred to Pakri police station but had not yet been relieved from his old posting because of Chhath festival arrangements. On Saturday evening, he had left police station by informing colleagues that he was going to his duty point.After postmortem examination the mortal remain of Kumar was brought to the police lines, where following guard of honours officials paid tributes and observed silence for two minutes.The officials also consoled Kumar's family, which also remained at police lines.

Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him. Article Title: 'Gurnoor Brar can take Prasidh Krishna's place': Sunil Gavaskar on India's bowling combination for NZ Tests
Article Text:
Gurnoor Brar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes Gurnoor Brar's inclusion in India's squad for the two-Test series against New Zealand is a decision driven by conditions, with the former opener suggesting the pacer could get an opportunity if Prasidh Krishna is not fully fit.Brar was drafted into the squad in place of wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav , with the team management seemingly looking to add pace and bounce to its bowling options for the challenging conditions in New Zealand. Gavaskar feels the move is also linked to concerns over Krishna's match readiness after his injury layoff.Krishna has not played competitive cricket since suffering an injury during the second ODI against West Indies in Guwahati earlier this year. While his pace and ability to extract bounce offer India a different dimension, Gavaskar believes Brar could step in if the Karnataka pacer is unavailable."Kuldeep’s exclusion was purely condition-based, and Brar can take advantage of the pace and bounce on these pitches as we saw in the ODIs. Also, Prasidh Krishna is coming in without much match practice off his injury, and so he may not be fully ready. Brar has been playing and is match-ready, and is perhaps why he has been included so that he can take Prasidh Krishna’s place," Gavaskar said on Sony Sports.The former India opener also weighed in on India's batting combination, backing Devdutt Padikkal to retain the No.3 position following his impressive performances in the previous Test series against Sri Lanka.Padikkal scored two centuries in two matches against Sri Lanka and also impressed in the warm-up games, strengthening his case for the crucial position. His inclusion comes at the expense of Sai Sudharsan, who had been given opportunities in the format but has yet to establish consistency.Gavaskar believes Padikkal has done enough to make the position his own, while Sudharsan would benefit from spending more time in the longer format."Padikkal has secured the No.3 position with the way he batted in Sri Lanka and even in the warm-up matches. Sai Sudharsan has been up and down in Tests. He needs more experience to solidify himself in Test cricket," Gavaskar said.Padikkal, meanwhile, has credited his conversations with Gavaskar over the years for helping him develop greater clarity about his batting approach and the demands of Test cricket."Obviously, I’ve had a lot of conversations with him over the years in terms of batting and what it takes to really spend long hours out there. Again, it comes back to preparation and understanding what you want to do. As long as you have that clarity in your head about what your plans are and what you want to go out there and do, regardless of the position you’re batting at, it helps a lot. I think those are the conversations I’ve had with him," Padikkal said in an interview with Star Sports.India begin their two-Test series against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday, November 19. The series carries significant importance for India's World Test Championship campaign, with both matches offering an opportunity to strengthen their position in the race for a place in the final.India have not won a Test in New Zealand since their 10-wicket victory in Hamilton in 2009. With the hosts currently among the leading contenders in the World Test Championship standings, Shubman Gill's side will be looking to overcome that difficult record and keep their qualification hopes on track.
Article Summary: Sunil Gavaskar believes Gurnoor Brar's inclusion in India's squad is a decision driven by conditions. Brar could get an opportunity if Prasidh Krishna is not fully fit. Former India captain backs Devdutt Padikkal to retain the No.3 position.

Article Title: Arnold Schwarzenegger bought the M47 Patton tank he once drove during Austrian military service; the 46-tonne Cold War vehicle later became part of his Hollywood life and even featured in a Netflix st
Article Text:
Image: Tork Buzz

Arnold Schwarzenegger served as an M47 tank driver in Austria

Austrian Army dug up and restored the tank for him

Schwarzenegger drove his personal tank over a Mercedes-Benz for Netflix

What is the M47 Patton tank?

M47 Patton was used by several countries during the Cold War

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Schwarzenegger uses the tank to raise money for charity

Hollywood actor Arnold Schwarzenegger owns an unusual reminder of his early years, a 46-tonne M47 Patton tank that he once operated during compulsory military service in Austria. The actor served as a tank driver at the Belgier barracks in Graz between 1965 and 1966, when he was 18. Decades later, he purchased the same military vehicle from the Austrian armed forces and brought it to the US. The Cold War-era tank subsequently became part of his public persona and attracted attention through his association with it. In 2023, Schwarzenegger even drove the vehicle over a Mercedes-Benz in a Netflix promotional stunt, using his personal tank for the announcement of his role as the streaming platform's Chief Action Officer.Schwarzenegger completed his compulsory military service in the Austrian armed forces between October 1965 and June 1966. According to the Austrian Ministry of Defence, he was stationed at the Belgier barracks in Graz, where he served as a driver of an M47 Patton tank.During his service, Schwarzenegger also experienced an unusual accident involving the vehicle. Recalling the incident during a visit to his former barracks in August 2012, he explained that he had been conducting a routine check on the tank when he failed to notice that it was in reverse gear.The vehicle consequently moved backwards through the brick wall of a garage. Schwarzenegger later recalled the incident as a small accident from his military days.The Austrian Ministry of Defence confirmed that he eventually purchased his former tank from the armed forces in 1994.The story behind how Schwarzenegger recovered his former military vehicle is unusual. After his military service ended, the Austrian Army had buried the tank as part of a decommissioning process.According to Netflix Tudum, Schwarzenegger later contacted the Austrian military and expressed his interest in acquiring the vehicle. The army subsequently dug it up, restored it and transferred it to him.He eventually brought the tank from Austria to the US, where it remained part of his personal collection.Schwarzenegger has also spoken about using the tank's storage space to keep weights and dumbbells during his military service. He would work out between drills, continuing his bodybuilding training even while serving in the army.In May 2023, Schwarzenegger brought his M47 Patton tank into the spotlight through a promotional video announcing his appointment as Netflix's Chief Action Officer.The video showed the actor driving the 46-tonne military vehicle over a Mercedes-Benz outside Netflix's offices. The stunt was part of the streaming platform's promotional campaign for its 2023 action-film and television lineup.In an interview with Netflix Tudum, Schwarzenegger confirmed that he personally operated the tank rather than allowing a stunt driver to take control."Was it really me driving? Of course it was. I wasn't going to let someone else have that fun," he said.The stunt reportedly took just two takes, with the tank crushing two different cars during filming. A stunt team that had worked with Schwarzenegger for around 30 years supported the production.He explained that he was particularly keen to use his personal M47 because it was the exact same tank he had driven as an 18-year-old in the Austrian Army.The M47 Patton was an American medium tank developed during the early years of the Cold War. Its development accelerated following the outbreak of the Korean War in 1950, when the US Army sought a more capable armoured vehicle to counter newer Soviet tanks.The vehicle was developed by combining a modified turret from the T42 tank with the existing hull of the M46 Patton. It was equipped with a 90mm main gun and a stereoscopic rangefinder designed to improve targeting accuracy.According to The Tank Museum, production of the M47 ran from July 1951 to November 1953, with 8,576 units manufactured by the American Locomotive Company and the Detroit Tank Arsenal.The tank weighed approximately 46 tonnes and was powered by an 810-horsepower, 12-cylinder petrol engine. It could reach speeds of up to 30 mph (48 km/h) on suitable terrain and had an operating range of approximately 80 miles.It required a crew of five, including a driver, assistant driver, gunner, loader and commander.Although the M47's service with the US military was relatively short, the vehicle continued operating in several countries after being supplied to American allies.The US Army began replacing it with the M48 Patton from 1953, and the M47 was declared obsolete in 1957. However, several countries continued using the tank for decades.Its international operators included Austria, Belgium, France, Italy, Pakistan, South Korea, Turkey, Iran and West Germany.The vehicle also saw combat in several conflicts, including the 1965 India-Pakistan War, the 1967 Six-Day War and the Iran-Iraq War of 1980-88.According to The Tank Museum, Pakistan deployed M47 tanks against Indian forces during the 1965 conflict, including in the major armoured battles at Asal Uttar and Chawinda.Beyond its military history and Hollywood appearances, Schwarzenegger's M47 has also been used to support charitable causes.Netflix reported that the actor uses his personal tank to raise money for charity. The vehicle has become a distinctive part of his public identity, connecting his early military experience with his later career as an actor and public figure.Schwarzenegger has previously spoken about his attachment to the vehicle, particularly because it represents a period when he was balancing compulsory military service with his ambitions in bodybuilding.
Article Summary: Arnold Schwarzenegger served as a tank driver in Austria between 1965 and 1966. He purchased the M47 Patton tank from the Austrian armed forces in 1994. In 2023, he drove the vehicle over a Mercedes-Benz in a Netflix promotional stunt.

Article Title: Theatre review: When the Ramayana looks beyond the familiar
Article Text:
A still from the play

Ramayana

Ram - The Musical Saga

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Should you watch it?

Ram - The Musical Saga

is at its most engaging when it looks beyond the familiar spectacle, even if the script itself could have benefitted from some pruning.





The tale of thehas been told countless times, and one often wonders what new possibilities it can still offer after decades of retelling across different media. However,, based on actor-writer Ashutosh Rana 's book Ramrajya, finds an interesting perspective to bring to the stage. The musical drama, directed by Rahull R Bhuchar, shines brightest when it steps away from the familiar narrative and brings into focus the motivations and dilemmas of its characters.The play begins with Lord Shiva narrating the story of Lord Ram's birth to his wife and Goddess Parvati. The well-thought out and period-appropriate costumes and Shiva's stately presence immediately grab attention.Ram's birth is celebrated with an elaborate dance sequence, brought alive by dancers' light footwork and Manoj Tiwari's singing. The actors playing Ram and Sita share an easy onstage chemistry. However, actor Aarav Choudhary, known for playing Bhishma Pitamah in the serial Mahabharat (2013), has a somewhat muted entrance as Parshuram. But the actor more than makes it up with his commanding stage presence and dialogue delivery.The musical works best when it veers away from the popular retellings and instead turns the spotlight on the possible reasons behind the choices of some of its key and often debated characters.Take, for instance, its depiction of Kaikeyi. The play implies that the decision to banish Ram to the forest was not hers alone, but that she was asked to own that part by Ram so that his father could keep his vow of giving her son the throne. The sequence has an emotional depth that some of the more familiar episodes lack.Other interesting departures include the inclusion of Shabari's devotion to Ram, as well as an episode in which Lord Hanuman, despite his undying loyalty to the deity, has to confront his own ego.The treatment of Ravan is particularly interesting. The writing explores the many layers that make up his personality -- his devotion to Shiva, his awareness about dying at the hands of a God, and his ability to question his actions. Even Mandodari, his favourite queen, is given a voice, as she questions his decision to abduct Sita.The songs and music have a pleasant quality about them, while the costumes, especially Ravan's scarlet-gold attire add to the visual appeal. However, music could have been used more effectively to move the narrative forward. The segments establishing the Ramanathaswamy Temple, Hanuman's entrance and even Ravan's sitar-playing could all have been trimmed.The conclusion features a 7-10 minute monologue wherein Ram addresses himself as the audience's friend and offers explanations behind his decision to separate from Sita and his children, Luv and Kush. However, they aren't entirely convincing.-Anvita Singh
Article Summary: Ram - The Musical Saga is based on actor-writer Ashutosh Rana's book Ramrajya. The musical drama shines brightest when it steps away from the familiar narrative. The actors playing Ram and Sita share an easy onstage chemistry. The treatment of Ravan is particularly interesting.

Article Title: Grandfather's trust, grandson's loot: How Delhi man with his friend siphoned off Rs 29.5 lakh from 87-year-old Navy veteran
Article Text:
Police arrested grandson and accomplice.

NEW DELHI: At an age when he should have been able to count on his family for care and companionship, an 87-year-old retired Indian Navy personnel allegedly fell victim to a betrayal at home. His own grandson, police said, allegedly used his grandfather's banking details to siphon off Rs 29.5 lakh, spending the money on holidays, parties and other personal indulgences.The alleged fraud, which continued for nearly seven months between April and October this year, came to light after the elderly man's son approached the police with a complaint about suspicious withdrawals and deductions from his father's bank account. An investigation by East district police eventually led them to the victim's 22-year-old grandson, Abhishek Raghav, and his associate, Tushar Chaudhary, also 22. Both have been arrested.What makes the case particularly disturbing is the alleged manner in which the money was siphoned off. DCP (East) Rajeev Kumar said Abhishek had linked his mobile number to his grandfather's bank account and allegedly exploited the access to carry out transactions in connivance with Tushar.Following the money trail, investigators found that Rs 9.2 lakh had been transferred to an India Post Payments Bank account held by Abhishek, while Rs 20.2 lakh was transferred to Tushar's account.The alleged spending spree that followed included trips to Manali, Nainital and Odisha, parties with friends in Noida and other extravagant personal expenses. The duo also allegedly purchased a car for Rs 2.7 lakh and spent another Rs 1.2 lakh installing a music system in it.The police team tracked the accused to Bulandshahr in Uttar Pradesh after analysing banking records, KYC documents and financial transactions. Two mobile phones and the car allegedly purchased with the cheated money have been recovered.Abhishek, who is pursuing a BA LLB degree from Khurja, is the son of the complainant and grandson of the victim. Tushar is pursuing a nursing course. Police have obtained their custody remand to trace the remaining money, establish the complete financial trail and identify whether anyone else was involved.
Article Summary: Retired Indian Navy personnel, 87, allegedly fell victim to a betrayal at home. His own grandson, 22, allegedly used his grandfather's banking details to siphon off Rs 29.5 lakh. The alleged fraud continued for nearly seven months between April and October this year.

NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department ( IMD ) has forecast thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and rainfall across several states over the next few days. Cyclonic Storm Akvan is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to parts of Andhra Pradesh Odisha and neighbouring states. Meanwhile, dense fog is likely to affect Delhi-NCR and adjoining northern states.The IMD has forecast dense fog at isolated places over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab until November 20. East and West Uttar Pradesh are also likely to experience dense fog during this period.The weather department has not provided a specific temperature forecast for Delhi in its latest bulletin.Cyclonic Storm Akvan, currently over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by November 19.According to the IMD, the system is expected to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20.At the time of landfall, the storm is likely to bring maximum sustained winds of 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.The IMD has issued an Orange Message cyclone alert for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts.In coastal Andhra Pradesh, light to moderate rainfall is likely at several places, with heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 18.Extremely heavy rainfall, exceeding 21 cm, is likely at isolated places over north coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20.The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at some places in Odisha, with heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 18.Rainfall is likely to intensify between November 19 and 21, with light to moderate showers at most places and heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated locations.Meanwhile, the Rayagada district administration has identified around 55 landslide-prone villages for possible evacuation and stepped up preparedness ahead of Cyclone Akvan.Located along the Andhra Pradesh border, Rayagada has been issued yellow and orange warnings for November 19 and 20, with heavy rainfall expected.Assam and Meghalaya are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall between November 19 and 22. Isolated thunderstorms and lightning are also expected over the two states on November 18 and 19.Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura may experience isolated to scattered rainfall on November 22. Thunderstorms and lightning are likely over these states on November 19 and 20.The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at many places over north Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 17 and 20, with heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 19.The rainfall could lead to waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu.Cyclone Akvan is also likely to influence weather conditions in Telangana after crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast.Four eastern districts of Telangana have been placed under an orange alert for November 20, with the possibility of heavy rainfall as the cyclonic system moves inland.The IMD said Cyclone Akvan was located approximately 610 km east of Chennai, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.The system is likely to continue moving northwestwards before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm.The IMD has advised authorities and residents in the coastal regions covered by the warnings to remain alert and follow official advisories.
Article Summary: Cyclone Akvan is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm. Affected areas include Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, experiencing heavy rainfall. Dense fog is likely to affect Delhi-NCR and adjoining northern states. Thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and rainfall across several states.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party leader Saurav Das on Tuesday said he had finally got his residential address in Delhi verified by the special executive magistrate (SEM), questioning why the Delhi Police had taken a month to complete the process.The verification came amid a dispute over the handling of his personal details. Das alleged that documents he submitted during the hearing, despite assurances that they would remain confidential, could end up being leaked and circulated among social media trolls.In a post on X, he said he had agreed to submit the documents only after the SEM accepted his condition that they be used exclusively to establish his residential address."During today’s hearing before the SEM Court, I submitted certain documents for verification of my residential address, on the express condition that they would not be leaked by the Delhi Police, only to eventually find their way into the hands of Rs 2 trolls for yet another round of false and nonsensical right-wing propaganda," he wrote.Das also questioned the police's delay in completing the verification, pointing to what he described as an earlier leak of his address, visits by YouTubers to his residence and pictures of a Diwali party at his home circulating online."It is remarkable that for the past one month, a Delhi Police force of over 1 lakh personnel has apparently been unable to establish where I live in Delhi," he said.Speaking to reporters after the hearing, Das said the matter had been taken up specifically to establish his current address. He said they had waited around two hours for the judge to arrive before the proceedings began."It is a matter of fact that the Delhi Police is aware where I live, but they have not been able to verify where I live. We came here to verify that; I am happy to announce it has now been verified," he said.Das and fellow party leader Ashutosh Ranka appeared before SEM Assistant Commissioner of Police Ritu Raj at Mandir Marg police station on Tuesday. Their sureties and supporting documents were also taken up for verification.The proceedings stem from their release from judicial custody on October 21. Both had furnished personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each and given undertakings to maintain peace and not call for protests at Jantar Mantar while it remained a denotified protest site.At a hearing on October 23, the SEM had asked Das to provide verifiable documents establishing his current residential address in Delhi.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party leader Saurav Das says he has finally got his residential address in Delhi verified. The verification came amid a dispute over the handling of his personal details. Das alleged that documents he submitted during the hearing could end up being leaked and circulated among social media trolls.

Article Title: Theatre director Salim Arif gets Ghalib Award
Article Text:
Mumbai:

City-based noted playwright, theatre director and costume designer Salim Arif has been chosen for prestigious Ghalib Award for 2026 by New Delhi-based Ghalib Institute. Among his other works, Arif (60) is known for collaborating with eminent poet-lyricist and director Gulzar on over a dozen projects, including the critically acclaimed ‘Tera Bayan Ghalib’, a theatrical and narrative journey of the 19th-century iconic Urdu and Persian poet Mirza Ghalib through his letters and poems.Arif has also designed costumes for several television dramas and films, including Gulzar’s Mirza Ghalib (1988) and Shyam Benegal’s television series Bharat Ek Khoj (Discovery of India) in the early 1980s.“The award consists of a cash prize of Rs 75000, a shield and citation. It will be given on December 18 in Delhi,” said a release from Ghalib Institute on Monday.A Lucknow University graduate and a National School of Drama (NSD) alumnus, Arif has lived and worked in Mumbai for over four decades.“The award is special because it is named after Ghalib. It is through Ghalib that I came in touch with Gulzar sahab,” said Arif. Gulzar had seen him work with Benegal on Discovery of India and asked him to design costumes for the Mirza Ghalib serial where Naseeruddin Shah played the protagonist, making Ghalib a household name.“Our show on Ghalib is also a tribute to Ghazal maestro Jagjit Singh who had agreed to sing some of Ghalib’s ghazals but died before he could record. We used Ghalib’s ghazals he had previously sung for the serial,” said Arif.He credited Gulzar for making Mumbai his home as “It was Gulzar sahab who asked me to stay back and I never left Mumbai.”
Article Summary: Salim Arif has been chosen for prestigious Ghalib Award for 2026. Arif (60) is known for collaborating with eminent poet-lyricist and director Gulzar on over a dozen projects. He has also designed costumes for several television dramas and films, including Shyam Benegal’s Bharat Ek Khoj.

Article Title: Techie back from Germany, 2 friends run riot at minister’s bungalow after drinking 23 beers
Article Text:

CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: The family of the Germany-based engineer, arrested with two others for allegedly causing a drunken ruckus at guardian minister Sanjay Shirsat’s bungalow on Thursday night, did not know he had returned to India over a month back and had been staying with friends while partying, police investigations have revealed.The accused, engineer Rohit Swapnil Bhutale (24), Shivam Dnyaneshwar Gaikwad (24) and Pratik Changdev Kute (25), were remanded to magisterial custody after completing a day in police remand, Satara police inspector Krishnakumar Shinde said.“During interrogation, the accused told us that the three of them had collectively consumed 23 bottles of beer on the day of the incident. The investigation also revealed that neither Bhutale’s parents nor any of his family members were aware that he had returned to India over a month back. He was staying with his friends,” the officer said.Police said Bhutale, a resident of N-1 Cidco, worked as a system engineer with a Germany-based firm. “He holds a master’s degree in cybersecurity. Gaikwad is an MSc student, while Kute, a BPharm graduate, works with a private medical coding firm,” police said.They have been arrested under sections 333 (house-trespass), 132 (assault or use of criminal force), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 351(3) (criminal intimidation involving threats of death, grievous hurt), 352 (intentional insult intended to provoke a breach of peace), 355 (misconduct) and 3(5) (liability for a criminal act committed by several persons in furtherance of their common intention) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.According to the FIR, the youths first hurled a liquor bottle at the bungalow and smashed another before being driven away by security personnel. They allegedly returned shortly afterwards and entered the premises through the main gate.Police said when police constable Vijay Bansi Darunte (52), who was on guard duty, along with private security guards and bungalow staff, tried to stop them, the accused allegedly pushed and abused them, threatened them and obstructed the constable from discharging his duties.One of the accused allegedly claimed to be an officer on special duty (OSD) and boasted of having contacts with senior officers. Darunte then dialled the emergency response number 112, following which a police team arrived and took the trio to Satara police station.
Article Summary: Rohit Swapnil Bhutale, Shivam Dnyaneshwar Gaikwad and Pratik Changdev Kute were remanded to magisterial custody after completing a day in police remand. One of the accused allegedly claimed to be an officer on special duty (OSD) and boasted of having contacts with senior officers.
